The lease clock and the resale market

Five charts for an article on HDB depreciation. 242,259 supplied transactions, January 2017–October 2026. A lease has less time remaining as it ages; observed market prices need not fall with it. These charts describe transactions and do not estimate a causal depreciation curve. October 2026 and the final year may be incomplete; the file’s extraction date is unknown.

Download every original record (CSV) · Methods & template selection

Prices rose while leases continued to run down

Annual median resale price · S$ nominal · one dot = one year · 2017–2026

Annual medians are transaction summaries, not an HDB price index. Changes in the homes sold affect this line. No inflation adjustment is applied.

The longest-lease band commands a higher median per square metre

2025 · remaining lease in years · S$/m² · each band includes every matching sale

The relationship is not monotonic below 80 years. This cross-sectional comparison does not isolate lease depreciation; town, model, storey and flat type are not controlled.

Lease bands contain widely overlapping prices

2025 · S$/m² · five-number distribution by remaining lease · hover for details

Whiskers extend to the furthest observed values within 1.5×IQR. All outliers are plotted; overlapping marks may coincide. No trimming or winsorisation is used.

Common flat types sold for more in 2025 than in 2017

Median nominal resale price · S$ · common flat types · matched calendar years, not matched homes

These are different transactions in each year, not the same properties resold. The rare 1-room and multi-generation categories remain in the full ledger and other all-record charts; they are omitted only from this common-type comparison.

The lease mix behind market prices changes each year

2017–2026 · bubble area = transaction count · columns = remaining-lease bands

All 242,259 records are counted exactly once here. The under-50-year band includes observed leases from 39 years 4 months. The final band has an exclusive upper bound of 100 years.
